name: spiny-back-beetle
artworkMethod: 16 individually generated painted cels; no animated part transforms or geometry interpolation
prompts: Use case: illustration-story. Production 2D game attack animation artwork. Create a STRICT 2x2 square grid containing exactly FOUR individually redrawn full-character animation cels on TRUE transparent RGBA background. Each cell is exactly one quarter of the square canvas. No text, labels, grid lines or shadows. Image 1 is the exact original character and style authority; image 2 is only a rough sixteen-pose motion guide. Redraw at much higher detail than image 2, preserving image 1's smooth painted rendering, crisp thin dark-teal contours, glossy burgundy shell, EXACTLY THREE large ivory back spikes, two ivory mandibles, amber eyes, six short articulated legs with dark feet. Each cel is a newly drawn coherent pose, not a transformed copy. Locked same front-left three-quarter camera and exact same scale and lighting across four cells. Preserve identical shell anatomy, proportions, spike shapes, shell color and markings in every cel. Character head points toward lower-left. Leave generous transparent padding: beetle visible art fills about 75 percent of each cell in width and 80 percent in height. Common rear-foot anchor and ground baseline. Whole character fits, no crop. In the animation the rear legs brace, head lowers, jaws open wide, front body lunges down-left and jaws snap shut, then recoils to the exact original neutral pose. Leg joints and jaw silhouettes must actually change with the pose. No invented extra body parts, no weapon or target, no effects, no smear duplicates, no white halo. These are animation SOURCE FRAMES that will be cropped into four equal cells. Read sequence top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right. Draw frames 1-4 of the complete sixteen-frame bite sequence. Top-left frame 1: exact neutral stance from original reference, mandibles relaxed with small gap. Top-right frame 2: slight lowering of head, front legs bend while rear toes planted. Bottom-left frame 3: deeper crouch, head drawn slightly backward, weight over braced rear legs. Bottom-right frame 4: low anticipation pose, head slightly back, mandibles opening outward with a much wider gap. This quartet only covers the smooth gradual beginning of attack.
